title: Mathematics — Grade 10 Entrance
subject: math

questions.prompt:
Safia has this rule.

> Start with the number n.
> Then cube the number.
> Then multiply by 7

Write down an algebraic expression for the rule in terms of n.

Write the correct index in each box.

1/5³ = 5^▢

6⁵ × 6⁻³ = 6^▢

(Type the two missing indices in order, separated by a comma.)

A polygon has 5 sides.
The polygon has 4 exterior angles each measuring 75°.

Work out the size of the 5th exterior angle of the polygon. Give your answer in degrees.

The diagram shows a quadrilateral drawn on a coordinate grid.

Draw the image of the quadrilateral after an enlargement, scale factor 3, centre (5, 4).

[This is a drawing task. If you cannot draw, state the coordinates of the vertices of the enlarged image instead.]
questions.criteria:
The original quadrilateral has vertices (2, 3), (4, 5), (7, 5) and (7, 2).
2 marks: correct image with vertices (−4, 1), (2, 7), (11, 7) and (11, −2).
1 mark: an enlargement scale factor 3 in the wrong position, or at least two vertices of the image correct.

questions.prompt:
The first term of a sequence is 3
The term-to-term rule of the sequence is 'square then subtract 5'

Find the 3rd term of this sequence.

Here is a distance–time graph for a journey.

Calculate the speed for this journey.
Give your answer in km/h.

A prism has a cross-section that is a regular pentagon. (Diagram NOT TO SCALE.)

(a) Find the number of planes of symmetry of this prism.

A prism has a cross-section that is a regular pentagon.

(b) The prism has a length of 15 cm. (Diagram NOT TO SCALE.)

The area of the cross-section of the prism is 10 cm².

Calculate the volume of the prism, in cm³.

Here are some measurements of length.

70 cm    500 nm    0.4 m

Write these measurements in order of size, starting with the smallest.

The diagram shows a shape made by joining a semicircle to a right-angled triangle.
The diameter of the semicircle is 22 cm.
The lengths of the perpendicular sides of the triangle are 22 cm and 31 cm.
(Diagram NOT TO SCALE.)

Complete the calculation for the total area of the shape:

1/2 × 22 × ▢  +  ▢ × π × ▢²  cm²

(Type the three missing values in order, separated by commas.)

Angelique records the resting heart rates for a group of people before and after taking part in a fitness programme.
Resting heart rate is measured in beats per minute (bpm).
The back-to-back stem-and-leaf diagram (see image) shows the results.

Key: 4 | 6 | 2 represents 64 bpm before the fitness programme and 62 bpm after the fitness programme.

The tables give information about six values that are missing from Angelique's diagram.

| Resting heart rate **before** fitness programme | Resting heart rate **after** fitness programme |
|---|---|
| Five values are missing. | One value is missing. |
| The minimum value is 49 | The range is 45 |
| The modal value is 78 | No person has a resting heart rate less than 48 |
| The maximum value is 97 | |

(a) Complete the back-to-back stem-and-leaf diagram with the **six** missing values.

[For digital answering: list the six missing values, stating which side (before/after) each belongs to.]
questions.criteria:
Missing BEFORE values: 49 (minimum), 78, 78, 78 (three more 78s so the mode is 78), 97 (maximum).
Missing AFTER value: 93 (min is 48 and range 45, so max = 93).
4 marks: all six values correct with correct sides.
Award 1 mark each for: 49 correct; 97 correct; three 78s correct; 93 correct (after side).

questions.prompt:
Angelique says,

'There is a greater spread of resting heart rates before the fitness programme compared to after the fitness programme.'

Choose the measure that shows Angelique is correct.

The time Pierre takes to solve a puzzle is 12.7 seconds correct to 3 significant figures.

Write down the lower limit for the time Pierre takes to solve the puzzle, in seconds.

Rajiv substitutes x = 3 into the expression 2x² and gets the answer 36

State whether Rajiv is **correct** or **not correct**, and explain why.
questions.criteria:
1 mark: states 'not correct' with a valid explanation, e.g. 2x² means 2 × (3²) = 2 × 9 = 18; Rajiv worked out (2 × 3)² = 6² = 36 (he squared 2x instead of squaring only x).
Both the decision and a correct explanation are needed for the mark.

questions.prompt:
Four students each start to solve a different calculation involving fractions.

For each student's work, state whether their statement is true or false.

Student 1: 7 ÷ 1/8 = 7 × 8

Student 2: 15 ÷ 3/4 = 1/15 × 4/3

Student 3: 27 × 2 5/8 = 27 × 2 + 27 × 5/8

Student 4: 3 5/7 × 6 = 3 × 6 × 5/7 × 6

(Answer for Students 1–4 in order, e.g. "True, False, True, False".)
Work out the value of (p⁵ + 10)/(3 + 2p) when p = 2

Youssef draws this table to record the length of each leaf in a sample of leaves.

| Leaf length (l cm) | Tally | Frequency |
|---|---|---|
| l < 10 | | |
| 10 < l < 20 | | |
| 20 < l < 30 | | |
| l > 30 | | |

Youssef has made some mistakes in the class intervals.

Write down class intervals that allow Youssef to record every leaf length.
Two have been done for you:

| Leaf length (l cm) |
|---|
| l < 10 |
| ______ |
| ______ |
| l ≥ 30 |

(Type the two missing class intervals.)

Work out.

(a) 1 − 7/10 ÷ 7

Give your answer as a fraction in its simplest form.

Work out.

(b) 1 3/5 × 4 1/8

Give your answer as a mixed number in its simplest form.

Solve the simultaneous equations.

3x + y = 14
5x + 2y = 25

(Give your answer in the form: x = ..., y = ...)

The diagram shows a triangle ABC.
ABD is a straight line. (Diagram NOT TO SCALE.)

The angle at A is 100°.
Angle x is acute and angle y is obtuse.

Find **one possible** pair of values for angle x and angle y, in degrees.

(Give your answer in the form: x = ..., y = ...)
questions.answerKey: x = 20, y = 120 (accept any pair with y = x + 100 where 0 < x < 80, e.g. x = 30, y = 130)

questions.prompt:
The diagram shows shape A and shape B on a coordinate grid.

Shape A is transformed onto shape B by a combination of **two** single transformations.
The first transformation is a rotation of 90° clockwise about (0, 0).

Describe fully the **second** transformation.
questions.criteria:
Expected answer: a reflection in the line x = −1.
1 mark: identifies the transformation as a reflection (single transformation only).
1 mark: states the mirror line x = −1.
No marks if more than one transformation is given for the second step.

questions.prompt:
Write the letter for each calculation in the correct place on the Venn diagram (see image).
One has been done for you: A is already placed in the 'Less than 8⁶' circle (outside the 'Equal to 1' circle).

A: 8² × 8²    B: 8² × 8³    C: 8¹⁵ ÷ 8⁵    D: 8⁰    E: 8 × 8⁵ × 8    F: (8²)³

The diagram has a circle 'Less than 8⁶' containing an inner circle 'Equal to 1', a separate circle 'Greater than 8⁶', and the region outside both circles.

(For each of B, C, D, E and F, state which region it belongs in.)
questions.answerKey: B: less than 8⁶; C: greater than 8⁶; D: equal to 1; E: greater than 8⁶; F: outside both circles (equal to 8⁶)

questions.prompt:
Jamila writes these rules about fractions and their decimal equivalents.

State whether each of Jamila's rules is true or false.

Rule 1: Fractions with an even denominator will **always** be equivalent to a terminating decimal.

Rule 2: Fractions with a denominator which is a multiple of 9 will **always** be equivalent to a recurring decimal.

(Answer for Rules 1 and 2 in order, e.g. "True, False".)

(a) Naomi has a bag containing 5 counters, each with a different **number** written on it.
She also has a bag containing 10 counters, each with a different **letter** written on it.
Naomi picks one counter at random from each bag.
One possible outcome is 3F.

Find the total number of possible outcomes.

(b) Naomi has these 5 white cards and these 3 grey cards.

White cards: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5
Grey cards: 2, 3, 4

Naomi picks one white card at random and one grey card at random.

Calculate the probability that both cards show a number greater than 3

It is given that

0.71 × 10ⁿ = 71    and    2.3 × 10ᵖ = 0.00023

Find the value of 0.067 ÷ 10ⁿ⁺ᵖ

Here is an algebraic statement.

(x + 3)² + c = (x − 3)(x + 5) + 4x

Find the value of c.

importNotes: Q18 (q21) has infinitely many valid answers — grader must accept any acute x with y = x + 100

Composite tick/fill-in questions (Q2, Q9, Q13 true/false, Q15, Q20 Venn, Q21) were adapted to typed multi-part short answers; auto-marking is order/format sensitive, AI near-miss checking should be lenient on formatting
Q10(a) stem-and-leaf completion is AI-graded against derived values (before: 49, 78, 78, 78, 97; after: 93) — worth a teacher spot-check
Q4 is a drawing task (paperOnly); digital students are told to list the image vertex coordinates instead
Source PDF (Cambridge 0862/01/O/N/24) has no cover page; durationMinutes=90 taken from the filename '1.5 hours'; no general instructions available.

Q2 (indices), Q9/no.8-style box-fill (no.9 area calculation), Q13 (four true/false ticks), Q15 (class intervals), Q17-style x/y answers, Q20 (Venn placement) and Q21 (two true/false ticks) were adapted from write-in-box/tick/diagram formats to typed comma-separated answers; auto-marker should be lenient about separators and wording.
Q10(a) (q11) was adapted from 'complete the stem-and-leaf diagram' to listing the six missing values with their side; graded as open_response with criteria (before: 49, 78, 78, 78, 97; after: 93).

Q4 (q4) is a drawing task (enlargement on a grid), marked paperOnly with an option to type image vertex coordinates; criteria give the expected vertices (-4,1), (2,7), (11,7), (11,-2) derived from the printed grid.
Q18 (q21) accepts many valid answers (any x, y with y = x + 80, 10 < x < 90); answerKey gives one example plus the rule, so teacher/AI review is advised.
Q13 (q15) has a single [2] mark for four true/false decisions and Q21 (q24) a single [1] for two decisions; per-item mark split is not printed in the source.
Q13 and Q10(a) attach full page renders (page-08.png, page-06.png) because the stimulus (four fraction work boxes; stem-and-leaf plus info tables) is split across multiple auto-cropped figures.
